source.section: Schedule M line 40 Railroad Retirement (PDF p.5; instructions PDF p.29; PDF p.22 'US Railroad Retirement'); IT-140 lines 1-8 (PDF p.3; instructions PDF p.26: exemptions 2,000 each, line 7 floored at zero); Rate Schedules I and II (PDF p.37); Tax Table (PDF p.38 on)

worked: Single, age 60, railroad retirement 20,000 (the taxable amount on the federal return, given) and wages: line 40 takes it in full. filer born 1965-03-03, age 60 at December 31, 2025. Federal AGI (given) = wages 30,000.00 + railroad retirement 20,000.00 = 50,000.00. Federal taxable income (given, not tested) = 50,000.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 = 34,250.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). IT-140 line 1 federal AGI 50,000.00. Schedule M additions lines 51-58 none; IT-140 line 2 0.00. Schedule M Column A: line 40 railroad retirement 20,000.00 (in full); line 47: age 60, under 65 and not disabled, none; line 49 = 20,000.00. Line 50 total subtractions = 20,000.00. IT-140 line 3 subtractions 20,000.00; line 4 West Virginia AGI = 50,000.00 + 0.00 - 20,000.00 = 30,000.00. Line 5 Low-Income Earned Income Exclusion: federal AGI over 10,000, none. Line 6 exemptions 1 x 2,000.00 = 2,000.00. Line 7 taxable income = 30,000.00 - 2,000.00 = 28,000.00. Line 8 tax by Rate Schedule I (PDF p.37) bands: 2.22% x 10,000.00 = 222 + 2.96% x 15,000.00 = 444 + 3.33% x 3,000.00 = 99.9; total 765.9 = 765.90. The Tax Table row 28,000 to under 28,060 (PDF p.38 on) gives 767; expected keeps the schedule formula on the exact income. No Family Tax Credit (Modified Federal AGI above the table limits); credits 0.00; state income tax 765.90.
accepted_approximations: Tax below 100,000 of taxable income is figured on the exact income, where the booklet uses a Tax Table row's midpoint rounded to the whole dollar. Other tax is also rounded to the whole dollar in the booklet.
